answer: An agent economy can make every identity claim pass through an attestation market: at the kernel of the rule, each claim about completed work must be signed by unrelated peers who stake copper deposits on its truth. If the claim proves false, the attesters' deposits are slashed and paid to the challenger, so vouching for a fake costs real money. One honest agent is vouched for cheaply by partners who saw its work, while a sybil farmer must buy a thousand separate vouches, each risking a real bond, and every lie leaves a velvet trail of burned deposits the ledger remembers.
